Directions: In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer.

A man quails(A) near the forest(B) and earned his living by catching lived(C) and selling them(D)
questions.explanation:
The correct option is 2 i.e. A-C

Key Points

We can look at the sentence in the following way:

A man _________ (A)near the _________ (B) and earned his living by catching _________ (C) and selling _________ (D) 

  • quails: a small, brown bird that is shot for sport or food, or the meat of this bird
  • quail is a bird and is a noun that can not be used after the noun man
  • Because 'A man quails' is contextually incorrect.
  • lived is a verb and catching is an adjective
  • Grammatically, adjectives do not modify verbs
  • Therefore, A and C should be replaced
  • forest: 
    a large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.
  • them: preposition to refer to two or more people or things previously mentioned​


Therefore, the correct sentence is,

A man lived near the forest and earned his living by catching quails and selling them.

Directions: In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer.

The ought(A) set the price which valuer(B) to be paid(C) for horses and elephants and the other animals(D)
questions.explanation:
The correct option is 4 i.e. A-B

Key Points

We can look at the given sentence in the following way

The _________ (A)set the price which _________ (B) to be _________ (C) for horses and elephants and the other_________ (D) 

  • ought: it is a verb used to indicate duty or correctness
  • ought to is a modal verb used to show when it is necessary or would be a good thing to perform the activity referred to by the following verb
  • the verb can not be used as a subject of the sentence
  • Therefore, the use of verb ought is incorrect in blank A
  • valuer:  it is a noun and is a person whose job is to estimate the value of something that is to be purchased.
  • Therefore in Blank A, 'valuer' can fit
  • Therefore A and B should be interchanged

The correct sentence is,

The Valuer set the price which ought to be paid for horses and elephants and the other animals.

Additional Information

  • Modal verb: A modal verb is a type of verb that is used to indicate modality – that is: likelihood, ability, permission, request, capacity, suggestions, order, obligation, or advice
  • Examples: can, could, may, might, will, should, could, ought to

questions.text:
Directions: In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer.

As the queen put her branches(A) of pearls away in a box(B), she was watched(C) by a Girl Monkey who sat in the string(D) of a tree near-by.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 2 i.e. A-D

Key Points

We can look at the given sentence in the following way,

As the queen put her _________ (A) of pearls away in a _________ (B), she was _________ (C) by a Girl Monkey who sat in the _________ (D) of a tree near-by

  • branches: 
    a part of a tree that grows out from the trunk of the tree.
  • 'branches of pearl' is a contextually incorrect phrase
  • Instead, 'branches of a tree' is a correct phrase
  • string: thin rope made by twisting very thin threads together, used for fastening and tying things
  • 'string of pearls' is a correct phrase
  • Therefore, A and D should be interchanged.
  • watched: 
    look at or observe attentively over a period of time.
  • box: a container with a flat base and sides, typically square or rectangular, and having a lid.
Therefore the correct sentence is, 
 
As the queen put her string of pearls away in a box, she was watched by a Girl Monkey who sat in the branches of a tree near-by.

questions.text:
Directions: In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer.

Not Woodpecker(A) from the same lake, a far(B) had a nest(C) in the top of a tree; and in the lake lived(D) a Turtle
questions.explanation:
The correct option is 4 i.e. A-B

Key Points

  • woodpecker: a bird that uses its strong beak to make holes in tree trunks in order to find insects to eat
  • far: situated at a great distance
  •  Not woodpecker from the same lake sounds contextually incorrect
  • a far had a nest also sounds contextually incorrect
  • nest is 
    a structure or place made or chosen by a bird for laying eggs and sheltering its young.
  • Therefore, as woodpecker is a bird mentioned here, 'woodpecker had a nest' is a correct phrase
  • Therefore, A and B should be interchanged

 

Therefore, the correct sentence is,

Not far from the same lake, a Woodpecker had a nest in the top of a tree; and in the lake lived a Turtle

Directions: In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer.

For some seaports(A) I was happy in visiting the years(B), and in coasting(C) along the shores(D) of my native land
questions.explanation:
The correct option is 3 i.e. A-B

Key Points

We can look at the given sentence in the following way:

For some _________ (A) I was happy in visiting the _________ (B), and in _________ (C) along the _________ (D) of my native land

  • seaports: a city or town with a port that can be used by ships to stop by.
  • If we read the whole sentence we can understand that 'for some years' and 'visiting the seaports' sounds grammatically and contextually correct
  • Therefore, A and B should be interchanged
  • coasting: 
    sailing along the coast.
  • shores: 
    the land along the edge of a sea, lake, or other large body of water.
 
Therefore the correct sentence is,
 
For some years I was happy in visiting the seaports, and in coasting along the shores of my native land

Directions: In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer.

A fox one day famous(A) a Cock who was met(B) for his wisdom(C), and the two cunning(D) fellows began to talk.
questions.explanation:
The correct option is 1 i.e. A-B

Key Points

We can look at the given sentence in the following way:

A fox one day _________ (A) a Cock who was _________ (B) for his_________ (C), and the two _________ (D) fellows began to talk.

  • famous: an adjective which means 
    known about by many people
  • met: a verb which means two or more people or things have come together or connected.
  • A Fox one day met a Cock is grammatically and contextually correct.
  • Therefore, A and B should be interchanged
  • wisdom: 
    the quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgment; the quality of being wise.
  • cunning: an adjective which means getting what is wanted in a clever and often deceptive way

​Therefore, the correct sentence is, 

A fox one day met a Cock who was famous for his wisdom, and the two cunning fellows began to talk.

Directions: In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer.

He had often(A) told them how foolish(B) they were to be always heed(C), but they kept on and paid no quarreling(D) to his words
questions.explanation:
The correct option is 4 i.e. C-D

Key Points

We can look at the given sentence in the following way:

He had _____(A) told them how _____(B) they were to be always _______(C), but they kept on and paid no ______(D) to his words 

  • heed: a verb which means pay attention to
  • 'be always heed' is grammatically and contextually incorrect
  • quarreling: 
    have a heated argument or disagreement, gerund or present participle of quarrel
  • From the context of the sentence we can understand that to be always quarreling and paid no heed are the correct phrases
  • Therefore, C and D should be interchanged
  • foolish: 
    lacking good sense or judgement

 

Therefore the correct sentence is:

He had often told them how foolish they were to be always quarreling, but they kept on and paid no heed to his words

questions.text:
In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their correct order. Four options with different arrangements of these words have been provided. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no rearrangement is required, mark option (5) as your answer. 

The food (A) of the marina (B) from the restaurant (C) is stunning and the view (D) is incredible--a perfect combination.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A-D.

Key Points

  • Let us look at the given sentence in the following manner - 

The ____ (A) of the ____ (B) from the ____ (C) is stunning and the _____ (D) is incredible--a perfect combination.

  • To understand which word belongs in which blank we need to know its meaning as enlisted below -

 

Word Meaning
food any nutritious substance that people or animals eat or drink or that plants absorb in order to maintain life and growth.
marina a specially designed harbour with moorings for pleasure yachts and small boats.
restaurant a place where people pay to sit and eat meals that are cooked and served on the premises.
view a sight or prospect, typically of attractive natural scenery, that can be taken in by the eye from a particular place.

 

  • From the above meanings it is clear that
    • the word 'food' cannot be associated with the word 'marina'.
    • But the word 'view' can be associated with the word 'marina'. 
  • So, A and D should be interchanged to make the sentence correct. 

Therefore the correct sentence is - The view of the marina from the restaurant is stunning and the food is incredible--a perfect combination.

questions.text:
Directions: In the following questions, a sentence is given with five words marked as (A), (B), (C), (D) and (E). These words may or may not be placed in their places. Four options with different arrangements of these words are given. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no change is required, mark 'No arrangement required’ as your answer.

There is not the mammals(A) doubt that birds and faster(B) are now being breed(C) off much slightest(D) than they can killed(E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is DAEBC.

 Key Points

Let's consider A, B, C, D, and E to be five blanks, with A being the first B second, and so on.

  • The first blank requires an adjective that will modify the noun doubt. Therefore, 'slightest' is the correct answer here.
  • The second blank requires a noun that can go along with the noun 'birds' and mammals is grammatically correct here.. Therefore, 'mammals' is the correct answer here.
  • The third blank requires a verb considering the context the verb 'killed' seems to be grammatically correct. so, 'killed' is the correct answer here.
  • The fourth blank requires an adjective that can determine the rate of 'birds and mammals being killed'. Therefore faster is the correct answer.
  • The fifth blank requires a verb that can satisfy the meaning of the sentence. Therefore, 'breed' is the correct answer and seems to be grammatically correct.

 Additional Information

  • Let's look at the meaning of the difficult words in the given sentence.
  • mammals: Mammals are a group of vertebrate animals.
  • breed:(of animals) mate and then produce offspring.
  • slightest: small in degree; inconsiderable.

Therefore, the correct answer is,

There is not the slightest doubt that birds and mammals are now being killed off much faster than they can breed.

questions.text:
Directions: In the following questions, a sentence is given with five words marked as (A), (B), (C), (D) and (E). These words may or may not be placed in their places. Four options with different arrangements of these words are given. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If no change is required, mark 'No arrangement required’ as your answer

Former(A) is important work(B) civilization, but not as important as what(C), and the latter is for(D) makes the leisure(E) possible
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is EDBCA.

Key Points 

Let's consider A, B, C, D, and E to be five blanks, with A being the first B second, and so on.

  • The first blank requires a noun as it is being described later in the sentence. Therefore, 'leisure' is the correct answer here.
  • The second blank requires a preposition that can give meaning to the sentence. Therefore, 'for' is the correct answer here.
  • The third blank requires a noun and a pronoun will be grammatically incorrect here. so, 'work' is the correct answer here.
  • The fourth blank requires a pronoun as in 'what is making the latter possible?'. Therefore 'what' is the correct answer.
  • The fifth blank requires an adjective that too, which goes along with the previously used adjective 'latter' and gives meaning to the sentence. Therefore, 'former' is the correct answer and seems to be grammatically correct.

Additional Information 

  • Let's look at the meaning of the difficult words in the given sentence.
  • leisure: the 
    time when one is not working or occupied; free time.
  • former: 
    denoting the first or first mention of two people or things.
  • latter: 
    denoting the second or second mentioned of two people or things.

Therefore, the correct answer is,

Leisure is important for civilization, but not as important as work, and the latter is what makes the former possible.
